english: Let $F:\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function such that $F'(x)=\dfrac{7\cos x-\sin x}{3\sin x+4\cos x}$ for all $x\in\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ and $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0^{+}}F(x)=\log_{e}4$. Then the maximum value of $F$ on $\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ is
hindi: माना कि $F:\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\to\mathbb{R}$ एक अवकलनीय फलन है जिसके लिए सभी $x\in\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ के लिए $F'(x)=\dfrac{7\cos x-\sin x}{3\sin x+4\cos x}$ तथा $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0^{+}}F(x)=\log_{e}4$ है। तब $\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ पर $F$ का अधिकतम मान है
solution: Write $7\cos x-\sin x=A(3\sin x+4\cos x)+B(3\cos x-4\sin x)$: $3A-4B=-1$, $4A+3B=7\Rightarrow A=B=1$
$F(x)=x+\log_{e}(3\sin x+4\cos x)+C$; the limit at $0$ gives $\log_{e}4+C=\log_{e}4\Rightarrow C=0$
$F'(x)=0\Leftrightarrow \tan x=7$; $F'>0$ before and $F'<0$ after, so the maximum is at $x_{0}=\tan^{-1}7$
solution_full: On $\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ the denominator $D=3\sin x+4\cos x$ is positive, and $D'=3\cos x-4\sin x$.
Write the numerator as $A\,D+B\,D'$: comparing coefficients of $\sin x$ and $\cos x$ gives $3A-4B=-1$ and $4A+3B=7$, so $A=1$, $B=1$.

$F'(x)=0$ exactly when $7\cos x=\sin x$, i.e. $\tan x=7$. For $\tan x<7$ the numerator $7\cos x-\sin x$ is positive and for $\tan x>7$ it is negative, so $F$ increases and then decreases: its maximum is at $x_{0}=\tan^{-1}7$.
With $\tan x_{0}=7$: $\sin x_{0}=\dfrac{7}{\sqrt{50}}$, $\cos x_{0}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{50}}$, so $3\sin x_{0}+4\cos x_{0}=\dfrac{25}{5\sqrt2}=\dfrac{5}{\sqrt2}$.
Therefore the maximum value is $\tan^{-1}7+\log_{e}\dfrac{5}{\sqrt2}$. Option (B) uses the wrong critical point and (C) the wrong sign of $B$.
originality_note: New: the antiderivative x + ln(3 sin x + 4 cos x) is not asked for; its maximum on an interval is, so the decomposition must be followed by a critical-point evaluation at x = tan^-1 7 (way 5). Closest known: textbook integrals of (a sin x + b cos x)/(c sin x + d cos x) by writing the numerator as A(denominator) + B(derivative). Different because: the question asks for an extremum of the antiderivative, with the constant fixed by a one-sided limit.
key_step: Writing the numerator as denominator + derivative of denominator, then evaluating at tan x = 7.
justification: A routine chain: one standard decomposition, a sign analysis and an evaluation. No insight beyond the standard method; comparable to 2023-P2-Q9 (L2), a solve-then-maximise question.
blueprint_concepts: Integrals of the form int (p.sin x + q.cos x)/(a.sin x + b.cos x) dx

concept_use.Integrals of the form int (p.sin x + q.c: The numerator is written as A(3 sin x + 4 cos x) + B(3 cos x - 4 sin x) with A = B = 1, which integrates to x + ln(3 sin x + 4 cos x).
concept_use.Integration of trigonometric functions: The integral of (3 cos x - 4 sin x)/(3 sin x + 4 cos x) is the standard trigonometric log integral, and its value at x = tan^-1 7 needs sin and cos of that angle.
